station: Just tell me what you'd do — advice at a health fair
why_this_one_now: The canonical competence-boundary station. Every school's version of Aston's published 'knowing your limitations'. Cheapest strong demo of the roleplay engine.

station: The relative who has been waiting
why_this_one_now: Anger plus clinical bait plus hidden information. The single best showcase station.

station: The lift home — a friend drove after drinking
why_this_one_now: Most realistic confidentiality station for a 17-year-old. Tests the promise-before-disclosure error that no static bank catches.

station: The bruise — a child at a youth club
why_this_one_now: Safeguarding done correctly: no investigation no promise named lead. High risk if built badly which is why it goes early with clinical review.

station: The message I forgot to pass on
why_this_one_now: Cleanest non-clinical duty-of-candour station. Discriminates on seconds-to-ownership.

station: Results day
why_this_one_now: Tests silence and refusal of comfort. Interactive-only behaviours that prove the engine is doing something a transcript cannot.

station: The teammate who stopped turning up
why_this_one_now: Hidden information gated behind an open question plus restraint. The hardest disclosure pattern and the most impressive when it works.

station: Before the results
why_this_one_now: Anxiety plus a request for a guarantee. Tests validating without false reassurance.

station: The fabricated placement
why_this_one_now: Peer misconduct with the candidate implicated. Mirrors QUB Station 1 which uses an actor playing a fellow student.

station: The consent form — a hesitant parent
why_this_one_now: Bridges roleplay and current affairs. Tests that the candidate does not argue the science.

station: Cancelled again
why_this_one_now: Legitimate anger where the candidate's organisation is in the wrong. Different demand from RP-001.

station: The spilled tea
why_this_one_now: Dignity under embarrassment. Tests behaviour the candidate must get right without the resident admitting anything.

station: DVLA — the patient who won't stop driving
why_this_one_now: The classic UK MMI confidentiality station AND a correction of a widely-taught error about who carries the legal duty.

station: A friend asks you to promise before they tell you
why_this_one_now: The non-roleplay twin of RP-010. Establishes the principle before the roleplay tests the behaviour.

station: You suspect something but cannot be sure
why_this_one_now: Teaches the single most unlocking principle in the domain: reasonable belief even if mistaken.

station: Two weeks later nothing has happened
why_this_one_now: The escalation-ladder station. Built entirely around the follow-up most banks never ask.

station: A capacitous adult refuses help
why_this_one_now: Tests the unwise-decision principle under pressure — the one candidates abandon when challenged.

station: Who gets the last funded place on the programme
why_this_one_now: Opportunity cost made concrete without requiring NICE knowledge.

station: The under-16 who does not want her parents told
why_this_one_now: Adolescent confidentiality plus the Gillick/Fraser correction. Requires clinical review.

station: Your supervisor asks you to do something you think is wrong
why_this_one_now: Challenging upwards. Pairs with RP-017 for the same topic in two formats.

station: A colleague makes a remark about a resident's family
why_this_one_now: Discriminatory comments. GMP 2024 Domain 3 content that pre-2024 banks miss entirely.

station: No harm came of it — do you still report it
why_this_one_now: Near-miss reporting and learning culture. Connects to the 2026 maternity findings.

station: Should a smoker wait longer for surgery
why_this_one_now: Desert-based rationing with hostile follow-up. Tests holding ground against an interviewer arguing the unfashionable side.

station: Which two principles are actually in conflict here
why_this_one_now: Purpose-built to score zero for naming the four principles and everything for identifying the tension.

station: Why medicine — and what nearly changed your mind
why_this_one_now: The most-asked question in UK medicine interviews. The value is entirely in the second clause and the follow-up chain.

station: Why not nursing or a physician associate
why_this_one_now: Tests real knowledge of adjacent roles. Live topic post-Leng and a red flag if answered by diminishing another profession.

station: Something from your work experience that changed how you think
why_this_one_now: Built on the MSC line: what you did is only half the story.

station: Tell me about a real failure and its cost
why_this_one_now: Automatic evidence probe on any humblebrag. Tests S4 directly.

station: What does a doctor actually spend the day doing
why_this_one_now: Realism check. Foundation band — early confidence builder that still teaches something.

station: What will you find hardest about training
why_this_one_now: Tests whether the candidate can name a real cost without performing sacrifice.

station: You said you're resilient — what's your evidence
why_this_one_now: The unsupported-claim trigger built as a station rather than only as a follow-up.

station: A time you supported someone else's decision you disagreed with
why_this_one_now: Deliberate followership prompt. Corrects the bank-wide bias toward leadership stories.

station: Should doctors go on strike
why_this_one_now: The tester named it. Symmetric challenge required. Hard expiry 2026-11-30.

station: Will AI replace doctors — and who is responsible when it's wrong
why_this_one_now: The tester named it. The accountability half is the differentiator almost nobody teaches.

station: Why do people in poorer areas die younger
why_this_one_now: The tester named it. Evergreen concept with a dated statistics layer.

station: Should the NHS fund weight-loss drugs at scale
why_this_one_now: Cleanest live rationing case with published cohort eligibility.

station: Should assisted dying be legal — and where is it now
why_this_one_now: Highest-salience ethics topic of the cycle. Hard expiry 2026-09-12 pending the 11 September Second Reading.

station: Is it fair to prioritise UK graduates for training posts
why_this_one_now: Directly affects the applicant. Handle with care — never signal a position.

station: Should we screen everyone for prostate cancer
why_this_one_now: Live NSC decision with a clean evidence-versus-advocacy structure and a usable false-positive figure.

station: Who loses when the NHS goes digital
why_this_one_now: Rewards connecting digital exclusion to the inverse care law — a link most candidates never make.

station: Explain a clinical trial to a ten-year-old
why_this_one_now: Comprehension checking with open questions. Low build cost high discrimination.

station: Describe it to me — the drawing task
why_this_one_now: Punishes closed checking by design. The listener says yes to 'does that make sense' regardless.

station: Tell someone their session is cancelled
why_this_one_now: Non-clinical bad news. The honest reframe of 'break bad news' for an applicant.

station: Explain to a member of the public what a waiting list actually is
why_this_one_now: Tests the boundary between lay explanation and clinical claim.

station: Apologise for something you got wrong
why_this_one_now: Apology without 'but'. Pairs with RP-015 in a different setting.

station: Five things to do and twenty minutes
why_this_one_now: Prioritisation where the criterion not the order is scored. Facts change mid-station.

station: You cannot do all of it — what do you drop and who do you tell
why_this_one_now: Deliberately impossible. Most banks make prioritisation merely hard.

station: Read this chart and tell me what it does not show
why_this_one_now: Limitations weighted above arithmetic. Directly serves Birmingham Imperial KMMS and Leicester.

station: Occupancy and discharge arithmetic — no calculator
why_this_one_now: Mirrors Leicester's published numeracy hurdle: GCSE level no medical knowledge no calculator.

station: A headline says risk rose by 50 per cent
why_this_one_now: Absolute versus relative risk. Highest-yield critical appraisal skill needing zero medical knowledge.
